_instructions: Fill in the real Villa Gjecaj tables and combinations, then run: npm run import:tables -- <path-to-this-file>  (add --confirm for a remote database). The importer is idempotent: it creates missing tables, updates matching ones (matched by name within an area), never deletes or duplicates, and reports any conflicts. Areas (Indoor/Outdoor) must already exist — run the bootstrap first. Nothing here is invented; leave the arrays empty until you have the real data.

table.name: string — the table's name/number, unique within its area (e.g. "1", "T1", "Terrace 3")
table.maxSeats: integer — the table's seat capacity (stored as `seats`)
table.minSeats: integer, optional — documentation only; the app has no per-table minimum

combination.name: string — unique within its area
combination.area: "indoor" | "outdoor" (all member tables must be in this area)
combination.priority: integer, optional (lower = preferred when capacities tie)
combination.tables: string[] — member table names, at least two, all in `area`
